about.title: Marine transportation, built up over more than sixty years.
text: Martin Marine is the marine transportation business of Martin Midstream Partners L.P., and its regional office is at 2904 N. 23rd St. in La Porte. We utilize a fleet of inland marine tank barges, inland push boats, and one offshore tug/barge unit to transport petroleum products and by-products largely in the Gulf Coast region.

Martin Midstream was formed in 2002 by Martin Resource Management Corporation, a privately held company whose initial predecessor was incorporated in 1951 as a supplier of products and services to drilling rig contractors. The current lines of business were developed and systematically integrated over a period of more than 60 years, including natural gas services and land transportation in the 1950s, sulfur in the 1960s, marine transportation in the late 1980s, and terminalling and storage in the early 1990s.

Our largest marine transportation customers include major and independent oil and gas refining companies, petroleum marketing companies, and Martin Resource Management Corporation. Additionally, our robust fleet contains vessels that reflect our focus on the transportation of specialty products.

facts.heading: Part Of Martin Midstream Partners
facts.text: Martin Midstream Partners L.P. is a publicly traded limited partnership with four primary business lines: terminalling, processing and storage; land and marine transportation; sulfur and sulfur-based products; and natural gas liquids, specialty lubricants and grease.

facts.heading: The Rest Of Martin Midstream
items: Terminalling and storage: 12 marine shore-based terminals and 9 specialty terminals
Land transportation: 23 terminals, more than 700 trucks and 1,200 trailers
Sulfur services and Martin Lubricants and Specialty Products

facts.heading: Gulf Coast Terminal Footprint
facts.text: Martin Midstream owns or operates 12 marine terminals along the United States Gulf Coast from Theodore, Alabama, to Port O'Connor, Texas, and is one of the largest operators of marine service terminals in the Gulf Coast region.

facts.heading: Named Terminals
items: Neches, a deep water marine terminal near Beaumont, Texas, on about 50 acres
Stanolind, on the Neches River in Beaumont, Texas, on about 11 acres
Tampa, on about 10 acres of land owned by the Tampa Port Authority
Ouachita County, on the Ouachita River in southern Arkansas, on about six acres
Three full service terminals, 13 lubricant and fuel oil terminals and 9 specialty petroleum terminals

facts.heading: Shore Base Support
facts.text: Full service terminals provide shore bases for companies operating in the offshore exploration and production industry, including storing and handling tubular goods, loading and unloading bulk materials, facilities from which oil companies communicate with and control offshore operations, and dockside facilities leased to companies providing drilling fluids and cementing services.
